title: Core ideas in art history
description: The movements, techniques and terms that help you see what a painting is doing.

ideas.title: Perspective and the Renaissance
ideas.summary: Renaissance artists used linear perspective and close study of nature to make a flat surface look deep and real.

items.q: In linear perspective, what is the vanishing point?
items.a: The point on the horizon line where parallel lines appear to meet

items.q: Which Florentine architect is credited with working out linear perspective in the early 1400s?
Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel between 1508 and 1512?
What is sfumato, the technique Leonardo da Vinci used in the Mona Lisa?
items.a: Soft, smoky blending of tones, with no hard outlines

ideas.title: Light and shadow
ideas.summary: Baroque painters used strong contrasts of light and dark to model form and heighten drama.

items.q: What is chiaroscuro in painting?
items.a: The use of strong contrast between light and dark to give figures a sense of volume

items.q: Which Italian painter, working around 1600, is known for figures lit dramatically against deep darkness?
Which Dutch master painted The Night Watch in 1642?
Which seventeenth-century style in European art is marked by drama, movement and strong emotion?

ideas.title: Impressionism
ideas.summary: The Impressionists painted the passing effects of light and weather with quick, visible brushstrokes.

items.q: Which painting by Claude Monet gave Impressionism its name?
In which city and year was the first Impressionist exhibition held?
What were the Impressionist painters chiefly trying to capture?
items.a: The momentary effect of light and atmosphere on a scene

items.q: What does it mean to paint en plein air, as the Impressionists often did?
items.a: To paint outdoors, directly from the scene

items.q: Which Dutch Post-Impressionist painted The Starry Night in 1889?

ideas.title: Modern art and abstraction
ideas.summary: In the twentieth century artists stopped copying appearances and asked what a picture, or art itself, could be.

items.q: Which movement, begun by Picasso and Braque around 1907, shows a subject from several viewpoints at once?
Who painted Guernica in 1937, in response to the bombing of a Spanish town?
What is abstract art?
items.a: Art that does not depict recognizable things, relying instead on color, shape and line

items.q: Which movement of the 1920s, including Dalí and Magritte, drew on dreams and the unconscious?
What did Marcel Duchamp call an ordinary manufactured object presented as art, like his 1917 Fountain?

ideas.title: Reading a picture
ideas.summary: Asking about medium, composition and symbols turns looking at a work of art into understanding it.

items.q: In art, what is composition?
items.a: The arrangement of the elements within a work

items.q: What is iconography in art history?
items.a: The study of the symbols and subjects in images and what they mean

items.q: What is a fresco?
items.a: A painting made on wet plaster, so that the color becomes part of the wall

items.q: On the traditional painter's color wheel, which color is the complement of red?
